chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashab, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf ibn Baqqah, from Mu'adh al-Jawhari, from Amr ibn Jami', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of your women is the one who is wholesome in food, pleasant in fragrance; when she spends, she spends with propriety, and when she withholds, she withholds with propriety. Such a woman is a worker among the workers of God, and the worker of God does not fail.'

key_terms.الطَّيِّبَةُ الرِّيحِ: Pleasant in fragrance — clean and fragrant in person
key_terms.الطَّيِّبَةُ الطَّعَامِ: Wholesome/good in food — skilled and excellent at preparing food
key_terms.بِمَعْرُوفٍ: With propriety/in a good and recognized manner — balanced, neither excessive nor deficient
key_terms.عَامِلُ اللَّهِ: Worker/agent of God — one who acts in accordance with God's will and earns divine favor

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the best of women?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a prophetic saying via a chain from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describing the qualities of the best woman: excellence in preparing food, pleasantness in personal fragrance, and balanced financial conduct — neither wasteful nor miserly. The Prophet concludes by elevating such a woman's status, declaring her a worker of God who will never be disappointed. In early Islamic society, these qualities reflected ideals of household management and moral virtue that were considered marks of a pious and worthy wife.
